Subject: Realtime streaming latency - BlueForge: acknowledgement & temporary fallbacks

Hi Alex / BlueForge ops team,

Thanks for flagging the elevated latency on streaming/chat endpoints this morning — I’m really sorry for the interruption. We’ve opened a high-priority incident and our on-call and account teams are working it now. Quick summary and immediate actions: 

- What we see so far: increased tail latency affecting streaming responses (partial token flushes and ~500-1200ms additional per-chunk delay) for requests routed to the us-west-2 edge tier.
- Impact window: starting ~2026-07-19T08:40 PDT, intermittent through now.
- Immediate mitigations we’ve applied: routing some BlueForge traffic to a lower-latency regional pool and enabling the standby model variant (quant-8 fallback) for affected routes to reduce kernel contention.

Practical temporary guidance you can apply on your side to reduce user-visible degradation:
- Retry/backoff: set transient streaming retry to 2 attempts with exponential backoff (200ms -> 600ms).
- Client throttling: lower the client-side max_concurrent_streams to 3 for now.
- Prompt slicing: if possible, trim long system prompts or truncate non-essential context to keep active KV sizes smaller.

We’re attaching the incident summary and the snapshot logs we collected so far. I’ll follow up with a technical write-up and ETA as we triage root cause. If you want a short call to coordinate fallbacks / canary routing, Marissa (cc’d) can spin up a bridge.

Again — sincerely sorry for the disruption. We’ll keep you updated every few hours or as new milestones are reached.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident technical summary: streaming latency (BlueForge)

Hi Alex / BlueForge ops,

Thanks again for your patience. Below is a concise post-incident technical summary and next steps.

What happened (short):
- Root cause: an unexpected scheduling regression in the serving runtime kernel selector combined with an edge shard queue hot-spot in us-west-2. The kernel regression caused increased context-switching on multi-tenant GPU instances, which manifested as higher tail latency for streaming token flushes.
- Impact window: 2026-07-19T08:40:00-07:00 -> 2026-07-19T11:05:00-07:00 (primary), with intermittent residuals until mitigations fully stabilized by 2026-07-19T13:30:00-07:00.
- Affected routes: streaming/chat endpoints for several customers routed to the us-west-2 edge; BlueForge experienced a higher-than-average hit due to session locality.

Actions taken:
- Immediately: routed 40% of traffic away from us-west-2, enabled quant-8 fallback, and applied conservative batching limits to reduce kernel contention.
- Fix deployed: rolled back the kernel selector regression and applied a patch to make scheduling decisions more conservative under high KV cache churn (deployed 2026-07-19T10:55:00-07:00).
- Post-deploy validation: ran synthetic streaming tests and real-customer canary checks; metrics returned to baseline within ~35 minutes after the fix.

Customer-facing mitigations you can use (already implemented / recommended):
- Client-side: set max_concurrent_streams to 3; retry attempts=2 with exponential backoff starting at 200ms.
- Server-side (Redwood): we can pin your routes to the dedicated pool for BlueForge for the next 72 hours to reduce session-locality re-exposure.

Permanent next steps (our roadmap items):
- Hardening: add unit tests for the kernel selector to catch regressions in scheduling heuristics.
- Observability: new metric for edge-shard queue saturation and an automated reroute when >80th percentile sustained for 5m.
- Architecture: consider stronger isolation for high-throughput customers (dedicated tenancy option).

Compensation / credits:
- Marissa has opened the credit review. We’ll follow Redwood’s SLA playbook and get you an initial credit proposal within one business day.

Logs and artifacts:
- Attached: redwood_incident_summary_20260719.pdf (customer-facing summary) and streaming-snapshot-logs.zip (sanitized logs). Full internal runbook and postmortem live in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_incident_playbook

Next steps on our side:
- Schedule a 30-minute incident review with BlueForge and Redwood infra to walk through the timeline and next steps. Marissa will coordinate times.
- Follow-up PR for kernel selector tests targeted for next sprint (ETA two weeks).

If you’d like anything else in the interim (more telemetry, deeper log slices, or a 1:1 technical session), reply here and we’ll prioritize.

Regards,
Dev Patel
On-call Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
